findings.title: stdout write in store library instead of the app's logger
findings.note: internal/store is library code (called from cmd/app/main.go), not a CLI entry point. main.go already uses the standard log package, so this fmt.Println bypasses the app's logging path and cannot be leveled, redirected, or captured in tests.

findings.title: No CI/CD automation to build, push, or deploy the Docker/k8s artifacts

evidence.quote:
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.22"
          cache: true
      - run: go test ./...

findings.note: The only workflow (ci.yml) runs go test and nothing else; there is no job that builds the Dockerfile image, pushes it, or applies the k8s manifests. Release/deploy is therefore a manual, undocumented step outside version control (docs/runbook.md and README.md do not mention it).

open_questions.question: The commented-out lint job at lines 17-20 — is this a planned addition or abandoned config? Not counted as a finding since it doesn't match the four listed symptom categories.

looks_bad_but_fine.why: Uses postgres:latest and mailhog/mailhog:latest floating tags, but this is a dev-only compose file, which is the documented trap (expected, not debt).
Non-dev compose file pins postgres:16.3 and redis:7.2, so no floating-tag or dev-path-in-prod issue here.

not_assessed: Whether the commented-out lint job in ci.yml reflects an intentional or abandoned decision (no doc or commit message evidence read).
Whether the curl | sh install step and privileged: true settings represent exploitable security risk — out of scope for pipeline-infra symptom categories and not assessed for CVE/exploitability here.
